about: Where each agent's hook contract was checked (Pulse reads no vendor file). Gate: scripts/catalog_check.py. Weekly sentinel: scripts/vendor_drift.py.

hooks.note: Every Pulse entry runs async: true — an async hook cannot block or decide ("Run hooks in the background": decision, permissionDecision and continue have no effect; only additionalContext and systemMessage are delivered, and Pulse prints nothing). PostToolUse is activity (tool_name + tool_input: the step; an Agent/Task call's step is its description, else subagent_type; a Skill's is skill; an MCP tool mcp__server__tool is "server · tool"); PostToolUseFailure (after a tool call fails; output cannot change the outcome) is activity too, except is_interrupt: true (the failure reached Claude as an abort) — a stopped line. UserPromptSubmit's prompt is the session's title. Stop's last_assistant_message is the last words (background_tasks / session_crons are not read); StopFailure's last_assistant_message / error_details / error is the turn's error. PermissionRequest is not a wait when nobody can be shown it: permission_mode dontAsk (in the payload), or a claude -p / --print process without --permission-prompt-tool (its argv, read by sysctl) — an ignored line "no prompt can be shown" (the doc: in sessions that can't show a prompt Claude still runs the hook and denies the call). AskUserQuestion reads tool_input.questions[0].question; ExitPlanMode reads tool_input.plan. Notification agent_needs_input fires for a background session while agent view is open, a teammate's terminal setup question or auto mode's classifier billing notice, and its payload (message, title, notification_type) does not name the waiting session: an ignored line "may be about another session". permission_prompt / elicitation_dialog / elicitation_url_dialog / idle_prompt / elicitation_complete / elicitation_response keep their meaning. PermissionDenied (auto mode denied a call) is installed async: its only control, hookSpecificOutput.retry, is a decision output an async hook never returns — a status line "auto mode denied <tool>" (tool_name only; reason is not read). PostCompact with trigger auto is a status line "compacted" (compact_summary is never read); trigger manual (a /compact at the prompt, no Stop follows) says nothing. SubagentStart / SubagentStop carry agent_id and agent_type: the subagent's own start and end of turn (a sub line: timeline only, it answers only that subagent's block, never ends or revives the person's turn); one without agent_id says nothing. Inside a subagent each event carries agent_id, written as the line's sub column. SessionStart's model and any token / cost field are never read. Silenced installs are said in Settings, read-only: disableAllHooks: true in ~/.claude/settings.json, or allowManagedHooksOnly / disableAllHooks: true in /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-settings.json or managed-settings.d/*.json. Never installed: PreToolUse, MessageDisplay, Elicitation, WorktreeCreate (each can gate or change what Claude does). Step facts (v9 cat / meta): PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure duration_ms ("Tool execution time in milliseconds") is the took column; PostToolUseFailure's error first line ("Key your hook on … the Exit code N first line") is meta err, bounded to 160 characters. A TodoWrite call's tool_input.todos[{content, status}] (Agent SDK TodoWriteInput; status pending / in_progress / completed) is meta plan=<completed>/<all> and planNow=<the in_progress item's content>; TaskCreate / TaskUpdate (one task each, no list) are plan steps named by their subject, without progress. A Skill call is a skill step named by tool_input.skill. Each tool's category is the adapter's table of Claude's tool names (tools-reference); mcp__<server>__<tool> is mcp. SessionStart's source (startup / resume / clear / compact / fork) is meta src; its session_title (a custom title: --name, /rename — a generated title is never sent) is the start's name, the row's title over the first prompt; UserPromptSubmit's session_title rides as meta name. SessionEnd's reason is meta why. SubagentStart / SubagentStop agent_type is meta type. Other hosts run Claude's settings hooks with payloads of their own — Cursor and its CLI (which import ~/.claude/settings.json; conversation_id + generation_id, cursor_version, camelCase hook_event_name) and VS Code (chat.useClaudeHooks; and Copilot's VS Code-compatible format: an ISO 8601 timestamp string): a payload with cursor_version, with conversation_id and generation_id, with a string timestamp, or whose hook_event_name is not the installed event is an ignored line "another host ran Claude's hook", never a Claude row.
unverified: The Cursor and VS Code payload shapes that run Claude's hooks (third-party bindings and VS Code's Local hooks reference, not Cursor's own docs)

hooks.note: Pinned at ce0323f (2026-10-17). hooks.json only — Pulse never touches config.toml, neither reads nor writes it (no notify argv; its allow_managed_hooks_only lives there and is not read). hooks.json shares Claude's nested shape and honours async (engine/discovery.rs: SessionEnd always runs synchronously, capped at 3 s; Interrupt runs async with its timeout capped at 3 s, written at the cap; an async handler's output is never read). PermissionRequest is never installed: it fires before Codex's own auto-review. Stop is the end of a root turn (last_assistant_message: the last words); a turn that ends on an error fires no Stop (core session/turn.rs returns before run_turn_stop_hooks) and nothing is inferred. UserPromptSubmit's prompt is the title; inside a subagent it carries agent_id and is the subagent's task, not the person's prompt. PostToolUse is installed async — the step (Codex says no tool start, so its row never stalls). SubagentStop (thread-spawned child turns; core hook_runtime.rs run_turn_stop_hooks) is installed async: agent_id is the child's thread id, session_id the root's — a sub line, timeline only, never the end of the person's turn. Interrupt (root turns only, TurnAbortReason::Interrupted; core tasks/mod.rs run_turn_interrupt_hooks; output only systemMessage) is a stopped line. Every thread of a session shares session_id; inside a subagent each event carries agent_id, written as the line's sub column. model / permission_mode are not read. Hook trust is bound to each entry's normalized text (discovery.rs hook_trust_status: Trusted / Modified / Untrusted): any change Pulse makes leaves its entries Modified and silent until trusted again in /hooks — Pulse does not guess at it; Settings says only that nothing was heard since the install, on a log that kept every line. SubagentStart (schema.rs SubagentStartCommandInput: agent_id, agent_type; its only output is additionalContext for the child — events/session_start.rs: "SubagentStart stays context-injection-only") is installed async: a sub start line, meta type. SubagentStop's agent_type is meta type. PostCompact (trigger auto | manual) is installed async: an auto compaction is a status line "compacted", a manual one says nothing. PreCompact is never installed: its continue: false stops the compaction (events/compact.rs should_stop). apply_patch's PostToolUse tool_input.command is the raw patch (handlers/apply_patch.rs apply_patch_payload_command): its *** Add File: / *** Update File: / *** Delete File: / *** Move to: headers (apply-patch parser.rs) are meta files (at most 16), the first the step's target (+N more). update_plan's tool_input.plan[{step, status}] (protocol plan_tool.rs; pending / in_progress / completed) is meta plan / planNow. Tool categories are the adapter's table of hook tool names (Bash, apply_patch, update_plan, spawn_agent…; hook_names.rs); mcp__ is mcp. SessionStart's source is meta src, SessionEnd's reason meta why.

unverified: conversation_id on every event (the session key; forum reports, not the docs)
postToolUseFailure fields failure_type (error / timeout / permission_denied), error_message, duration, is_interrupt
the agent's tool names (shell, read_file, edit_file…) behind each category
hooks.note: cursor.com was unreachable from the build environment (2026-09-29, 2026-10-17); event names and payload fields (conversation_id, workspace_roots, status, command, file_path, tool_name, text) were cross-checked against third-party typed bindings (pkg.go.dev/github.com/Checkmarx/ast-cx-hooks/cursor, github.com/speakeasy-api/gram server/design/hooks) and Cursor forum reports. Every before* event and beforeSubmitPrompt can deny or stop and is never installed. The session is conversation_id, read before session_id (forum reports: sessionStart carries both, the tool events only conversation_id). afterShellExecution (command; duration in ms when present), afterFileEdit (file_path, said relative to its workspace root) and afterMCPExecution (tool_name; the payload names no server) are the steps — they also fire in the cursor-agent CLI, where afterAgentResponse does not; output, edits, tool_input and result_json are never read. afterAgentResponse's text is the turn's last words so far. stop status completed is your turn, error a failed turn (no error text is sent), aborted a stopped turn. model, cursor_version and user_email are never read. Re-read the docs on a machine that can reach them: the duration field is not confirmed. postToolUseFailure (observational: no output is read — github.com/Checkmarx/ast-cx-hooks cursor/types.go ToolFailureEvent) is installed: a step marked failed with meta err = failure_type and took = duration; is_interrupt is a stopped line. sessionEnd's reason is meta why and its error_message first line meta err. The CLI's agent command is a link into ~/.local/share/cursor-agent/versions/…, matched by the cursor-agent path component; a bare agent outside it is never Cursor.

Pinned at 8efd314 (2026-10-16). User extensions load from getAgentDir()/extensions — ~/.pi/agent unless PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR moves it (src/config.ts); Pulse, a GUI app, follows no environment and installs to ~/.pi/agent, and Settings says so when that folder is missing on a Mac where Pi is present. Extension events are notifications when the handler returns nothing; before_agent_start, input, tool_call, tool_result, turn_end, message_end, user_bash and session_before_switch/fork/compact/tree can change what Pi does and are never subscribed. The extension sends nothing when ctx.mode is json or print (subagents run as pi --mode json -p --no-session, examples/extensions/subagent). Each event is one pulse-hook child, spawned only after the previous one exited (1.5 s guard; queue of 64, a block, its answer, the turn's end and the shutdown dropped last; flushed on session_shutdown), so lines are numbered in emission order. ui_prompt_start/ui_prompt_end (reason ui_prompt, kind, title) come from ExtensionRunner.withUIPrompt (runner.ts): confirm is a permission, select/input/editor a question (interactive-mode.ts setBlocked), custom is not a block and is an ignored line. Pi's own blocks that do not pass through it — the /login OAuth wait and the missing-session-cwd confirm (promptForMissingSessionCwd) — are not reported. tool_execution_start is sent as a status line (tool + one argument: command for bash/powershell, path for read/edit/write/ls, pattern for grep/find, else a fallback list) and its argument kept by toolCallId for tool_execution_end, which carries isError and durationMs (sent as is_error/duration_ms) but no args; calls with parentToolCallId (nested calls a tool made) are not sent. message_start is sent for role user only; a skill block (<skill name=… location=…>…</skill>, agent-session.ts parseSkillBlock) is sent as /skill:name args, never the skill path. session_start carries getSessionName(); session_info_changed (setSessionName) carries the new name. agent_settled carries aborted (an Escape: a stopped line); otherwise the run's last assistant words or errorMessage from agent_end (observed, never sent). The extension sends process.pid (accepted only as the hook's own parent) and no transcript path. Pi sets process.title to pi / pi-rpc (cli/setup.ts, rpc-entry.ts), which on macOS leaves argv ["pi", "", …] under node. session_start's reason (startup / new / resume / fork; types.ts SessionStartEvent) is forwarded as source — meta src; session_shutdown's reason (quit / new / resume / fork) is meta why. Tool categories are the adapter's table of Pi's built-in tools (bash, read, edit, write, ls, grep, find).

camelCase event names select the camelCase payload. Each entry runs the launcher directly: exec + args (CLI only, "Command hooks": no shell interprets the path), timeoutSec. notification is fire-and-forget, installed with matcher permission_prompt|elicitation_dialog|agent_idle (regex on notification_type); agent_idle/agent_completed describe background subagents and are not read as the session's turn. agentStop and postToolUse/postToolUseFailure are synchronous and could return a decision (agentStop decision: block; postToolUse modifiedResult) — an owner-approved exception: Pulse's hook appends one line, prints nothing and exits 0, so it never decides ("Return {} or empty output" keeps the original result). The tool ran, which answers a permission_prompt. postToolUse sends toolArgs as a JSON string; its command or path is the step's target. userPromptSubmitted's prompt is the title; sessionStart's initialPrompt (a -p run) is the session's name. subagentStart (cannot block creation; its additionalContext is never returned) is a status line marked with agentName — its payload carries no agentId. preCompact (notification only) is installed with matcher auto and is a status line "compacting"; a manual one is the person at the prompt. An unrecoverable errorOccurred ends the turn with error.message as its error; a recoverable one is a status line, which never starts a turn (it moves nothing once the turn ended). Inside a subagent each event carries `agentId`, written as the line's sub column (a subagent never answers the main agent's block, never revives an ended turn and is never the person's prompt). Hooks load from ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json, or $COPILOT_HOME/hooks/ — Pulse follows no environment and installs to ~/.copilot. With the session sandbox on, user hooks run inside it with the agent's own access: Pulse's folder (~/Library/Application Support/Pulse) must be granted in sandbox.userPolicy (~/.copilot/settings.json) or the hook cannot write its line — Settings then says the install has heard nothing. A recoverable errorOccurred is a status line "recoverable error" with error.name as meta err; postToolUseFailure's error first line is meta err. sessionStart's source is meta src, sessionEnd's reason meta why. Tool categories follow the runtime names (hooks-reference, Claude-format matchers: bash, view, create, edit, grep, glob, web_fetch, task, update_todo…); update_todo's arguments are not documented, so it is a plan step without progress. Silenced installs are said in Settings, read-only: disableAllHooks: true in ~/.copilot/settings.json (cli-config-dir-reference: "Disable all hooks (both repository-level and user-level)"); Copilot documents no managed-only switch, and policy hooks are not Pulse's.

One plugin file for both lines, in ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ (both scan {plugin,plugins}/*.{js,ts} under the global config folder: 1.x Global config, 2.x core plugin/source-directory.ts with util global-roots.ts). It exports only a default object { id: "pulse", server, setup }: 1.x readV1Plugin (plugin/shared.ts) takes a default with an id and server() and calls server — older loaders that walk every export accept an object with server too, so there is no named export (it would load twice); 2.x core plugin/module.ts decodes a default { id, setup } (or effect) and ignores the rest. 1.x: the event hook gets every bus event as { type, properties } (plugin/index.ts). 2.x: setup reads ctx.event.subscribe (plugin promise/adapter.ts: the bus encoded as OpenCodeEvent, { type, data, location }) until the plugin unloads; events of another location are skipped. Never a hook that can change what OpenCode does (tool.execute.before/after, chat.*, permission.ask, 2.x session/tool/permission hooks). Asks: 1.x permission.asked (id, permission, patterns, tool.callID) / question.asked (id, questions) answered by permission.replied / question.replied / question.rejected (requestID); 2.x permission.asked (id, action, resources, message, source.id — only when a rule says ask, core permission.ts) / form.created (form.id, fields[0].description is the question: question tool, MCP elicitation, websearch) answered by permission.replied (requestID) / form.replied / form.cancelled (id). The plugin keeps each root session's open ask ids and sends pending (still open) with each answer: Pulse clears the block only when none is. An ask names the asking tool from its call id when the call was seen. Subagents run in child sessions (parentID on 1.x session.created/updated/deleted info, 2.x session.created data); a child's lifecycle, prompts and steps are dropped, its asks and answers sent under the root id. Steps: 1.x message.part.updated tool parts — the first running state is a status line (what runs now), completed/error once per callID is the step (tool, one input argument, error, time.end - time.start); a call an abort interrupted (metadata.interrupted) is no step. 2.x session.tool.input.started (name; observed, never sent), session.tool.called (status) and session.tool.success / session.tool.failed (step; duration from the events' created clocks). Prompts: 1.x a user message (message.updated role user, observed) and its first non-synthetic text part; 2.x session.inbox.enqueued items of type user; 2.x session.execution.started also starts the turn. Titles: session.created title, 1.x session.updated info.title, 2.x session.renamed — not the default "New session - <ISO date>" (1.x session.ts isDefaultTitle), each sent when it changes. Turn ends: 1.x session.idle, 2.x session.execution.succeeded; 1.x session.error carries error.name: MessageAbortedError is a stopped line and the session.idle after it is not sent; ContextOverflowError is a status (processor.ts halt: with compaction.auto it compacts and goes on; with it off, session.idle follows); an error without a sessionID is an ignored line. 2.x session.execution.failed (error.message) is a failed turn; session.execution.interrupted reason user is stopped, inactivity a failed turn, superseded / shutdown say nothing. 1.x session.compacted, 2.x session.compaction.ended and session.retry.scheduled are status lines. session.status busy (sent when it changes) / retry are status lines: never a step, never an answer, never the start of a turn. No cost, tokens, model or usage field is read or forwarded. OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR (1.x: an extra folder; 2.x: replaces the global one) and XDG_CONFIG_HOME move where OpenCode reads plugins; Pulse, a GUI app, follows neither and says so when ~/.config/opencode is missing on a Mac where OpenCode runs. 1.x todo.updated ({sessionID, todos[{content, status}]}, schema session-todo.ts) is a status line "plan updated" with meta plan / planNow; session.diff ({sessionID, diff[{file, additions, deletions, status}]}, schema file-diff.ts; an empty diff is not sent) is a status line "N files changed" with meta files (at most 16). Archiving is session.updated with info.time.archived (there is no session.archived event on either line): the plugin sends session.updated with archived once, an end line (meta why archived). 2.x has neither event. A child session's tool steps (1.x tool parts, 2.x session.tool.*) are sent under the root with subagent_id = the child's id: the line's sub column. A skill tool's step names input.name. Tool categories are the adapter's table of OpenCode's built-in tools.
